title: ShipReel
transcript: Now that Hixfield has their own MCP and has kind of open source systems, what can we build through that? Like maybe a launch video, start SaaS where people just give them, give their startup context, codebase and stuff and instructions and/or prompt. For how do they like their launch video to generate. And we call Hexfield API and then generate their launch reel, launch video, launch demo. Maybe that can become a, you know, SaaS tool.

prd.oneLiner: The only fully hosted SaaS that turns a founder's repo, context, and launch instructions straight into a finished multi-format launch video via Higgsfield's API — no MCP setup, no CLI, no prompt engineering.
prd.problem: Indie founders launching on Product Hunt, the App Store, or X need a polished launch video fast, but agencies charge $1,000-$20,000 and take weeks, so most founders either skip video entirely or DIY it by manually feeding their codebase into Claude Design to extract a design system and then hand-prompting scene-by-scene footage — a process the community has documented as working but painfully slow and fully manual. The alternative, Higgsfield's open MCP ecosystem, gives technical users access to 30+ video models and ready-made UGC/faceless skills, but every existing wrapper around it — Higgsfield's own chat-based skills, reeljet, Higgsfield Director MCP, AI Promo Video — either requires freeform prompting inside Claude/ChatGPT, demands CLI and MCP setup, or targets generic ad/UGC content rather than a startup's actual codebase and launch narrative. None of them offer a single hosted flow where a non-technical founder hands over a repo, a prompt, and a platform, and gets back a finished, publishable launch reel.
prd.targetUser: Solo founders and small indie SaaS teams preparing a Product Hunt, App Store, or social launch who want an agency-quality demo video without learning MCP, Claude Code, or video editing tools.

must_have.title: Higgsfield video generation integration
must_have.description: Call Higgsfield's API/MCP models (Veo, Kling, Seedance, etc.) to render the launch video from a generated script and supplied assets.

must_have.title: Multi-format export
must_have.description: Output both a 16:9 master video and a 9:16 reframed vertical cut for Product Hunt, landing pages, and Reels/TikTok/Shorts.

must_have.title: Script and narrative generation
must_have.description: Generate a launch-video script and shot list from the founder's product description, instructions, and tone preferences.

must_have.title: Caption/subtitle generation
must_have.description: Auto-generate burned-in captions synced to the narration or voiceover track.

must_have.title: Screenshot/screen-recording ingestion
must_have.description: Accept uploaded product screenshots, screen recordings, and logo assets as real footage source material for the video.

must_have.title: Cost/credit visibility before render
must_have.description: Show estimated Higgsfield credit cost and require explicit approval before spending render budget on a generation job.

should_have.title: Guided intake wizard
should_have.description: Replace freeform chat prompting with a structured form for tone, style, platform, and brand preferences, better than Higgsfield MCP's raw prompt-driven UGC Factory.

should_have.title: Codebase-aware context extraction
should_have.description: Pull README, package.json, and repo structure to auto-generate feature lists and value props, beyond reeljet's screenshot-only ingestion.

should_have.title: Flat-fee credit abstraction
should_have.description: Bill founders one predictable subscription price instead of exposing raw Higgsfield credits, improving on Director MCP's manual cost-preflight approach.

should_have.title: Bundled publishing kit
should_have.description: Auto-generate a title, description, hashtags, and thumbnail alongside the video, saving the manual assembly step required in AI Promo Video.

could_have.title: Startup-launch-specific templates
could_have.description: Offer Product Hunt launch reel, investor teaser, and App Store trailer templates distinct from generic UGC/ad templates.

could_have.title: One-click GitHub connect
could_have.description: OAuth into a repo to auto-pull README and changelog content instead of manually pasting context.

could_have.title: Launch-specific hook scoring
could_have.description: Score generated cuts on hook strength and pacing tuned for launch-day virality rather than general ad performance.

wont_have.title: Mobile apps
wont_have.description: No native iOS/Android app; web-only for the 72-hour MVP.

wont_have.title: Voice/persona customization
wont_have.description: No custom avatar creation or voice cloning; use Higgsfield's default voices/avatars as-is.

wont_have.title: Advanced integrations
wont_have.description: No Zapier, Slack, or CI/CD pipeline triggers for auto-generating videos on deploy.

wont_have.title: White-labelling
wont_have.description: No agency/reseller white-label branding options at launch.

wont_have.title: Multi-language support
wont_have.description: No localized script or voiceover generation beyond English.

wont_have.title: Admin dashboard
wont_have.description: No team roles, analytics dashboard, or multi-seat account management.

wont_have.title: Fully custom code-generated motion graphics
wont_have.description: No Revideo/Three.js-level custom animation system like AI Promo Video; we rely on Higgsfield's model outputs, not bespoke rendering pipelines.

wont_have.title: Faceless long-form content factory
wont_have.description: No 10-minute YouTube explainer generation; scope is limited to short launch videos, not Higgsfield's Faceless Content Factory use case.

successMetrics.target: 150 founders sign up within the first 30 days post-launch
≥20% of signups convert to a paid plan within 14 days of signup, yielding ~30 paying customers by day 44
≥85% of launch-video generation jobs complete without manual retry within the first 60 days
≥4.2/5 average CSAT (5-point post-delivery survey) collected within the first 60 days

openQuestions: What markup on Higgsfield API/credit costs is needed to sustain a $69/mo flat fee without eroding margin?
Should GitHub repo OAuth be required at signup, or is screenshot-only ingestion sufficient for the 72-hour MVP?

Do we proxy/store rendered videos ourselves or serve directly from Higgsfield's storage for v1?

research.marketSummary: The launch/demo video space is rapidly being reshaped by Higgsfield's open MCP, which has spawned an ecosystem of official skills (UGC Factory, Faceless Content Factory) and a handful of small open-source projects (reeljet, Higgsfield Director MCP, AI Promo Video) that chain Higgsfield or code-based rendering (Revideo/FFmpeg) to automate promo videos for indie founders. Most solutions today are either generic ad/UGC generators requiring manual prompting, or developer-only open-source skills with no hosted UI, support, or business model. None combine deep codebase/context ingestion, a guided intake of founder instructions/preferences, and a fully hosted, non-technical SaaS experience purpose-built for startup launch videos.
research.ourPositioning: We are the first fully hosted, non-technical SaaS that turns a startup's codebase, context, and launch instructions directly into a polished, multi-format launch video via Higgsfield's API - eliminating the need to learn MCP, prompt-engineer, or stitch together open-source developer tools that today's Higgsfield ecosystem requires.
tableStakes: Integration with AI video generation models (Higgsfield MCP or equivalent: Sora, Veo, Kling, Seedance)
Support for common launch/promo formats (16:9 landscape and 9:16 vertical for Reels/TikTok/Shorts/Product Hunt)
Script/narrative generation from a product description or prompt
Ability to incorporate real product screenshots or screen recordings
Cost/credit visibility before rendering to avoid wasted spend
differentiationOpportunities: Native codebase ingestion (not just screenshots) to auto-extract product design system, features, and value props for accurate, on-brand video content
Fully hosted, non-technical SaaS onboarding (no Claude Code/CLI/MCP setup required) targeting founders who don't want to touch developer tooling
Structured intake of founder preferences/instructions (tone, style, target platform, brand guidelines) as a guided form/wizard rather than freeform prompting
End-to-end packaging: single click from 'give us your repo + instructions' to a finished, multi-format launch reel/demo/video with publishing kit (titles, captions, hashtags)
Startup-launch-specific templates (Product Hunt launch, investor teaser, App Store trailer) versus generic UGC/ad templates
Managed cost/credit abstraction so founders pay one predictable SaaS price instead of managing Higgsfield credits directly

logoDirection.form: Abstract play-button/film-reel hybrid formed from a code bracket shape
logoDirection.style: Modern geometric tech mark with subtle motion cues
avoidances: Literal clapperboard or camera icons (too generic/stock)
Overly corporate or agency-style crest logos
Complex gradients that don't scale down to favicon size
Anything resembling TikTok/YouTube's existing logo language
logoDirection.symbolConcept: A play triangle merged with a closing code bracket ']' to represent code transforming into finished video

brand.iconographyStyle: Flat geometric line icons with rounded corners, consistent 2px stroke weight, minimal detail, using bracket/play/frame motifs to reinforce the code-to-video narrative, subtle accent-color highlights on interactive states

engineering.overview: ShipReel is a hosted Next.js SaaS that converts a founder's repo context, uploaded assets, and launch instructions into a finished multi-format launch video by orchestrating Higgsfield's video-generation API. Users go through a guided intake wizard (no MCP/CLI/prompt engineering), the backend extracts context (repo README/package.json or manual input), generates a script/shot-list via an LLM, assembles a Higgsfield render job with uploaded screenshots/screen-recordings, previews estimated credit cost for approval, submits the render, polls/receives webhook status, then produces 16:9 and 9:16 exports with burned-in captions and a publishing kit (title/description/hashtags/thumbnail). Billing is a flat-fee subscription abstracting raw Higgsfield credit costs.
engineering.dataFlow: User signs up (Supabase Auth) → creates a Project via intake wizard, entering product description, tone/platform preferences, and uploading screenshots, screen recordings and logo → Context Extraction Service parses any supplied repo text/README into structured context → Script Generation Service calls the LLM to produce script + shot list + captions for review → user approves; Higgsfield Orchestration Service computes estimated credit cost for explicit approval → a render_job is enqueued → Job Worker submits to Higgsfield's API and tracks status → on completion, the worker fetches 16:9 and 9:16 outputs, burns captions, generates a thumbnail and publishing-kit text → the web app shows finished videos for download once status = completed.

components.name: Web App (Next.js)
components.responsibility: Guided intake wizard, asset upload UI, cost/credit approval screen, job status dashboard, video preview/download, account & billing settings.

components.name: API Layer (Next.js Route Handlers / Edge & Server Functions)
components.responsibility: Auth-guarded REST endpoints for projects, uploads, script generation, job submission, status polling, and webhook receipt from Higgsfield.

components.name: Context Extraction Service
components.responsibility: Parses uploaded repo metadata (README, package.json) or manual form input into structured feature/value-prop data used for script generation.

components.name: Script & Shot-List Generation Service (LLM)
components.responsibility: Calls an LLM to turn extracted context + tone/platform preferences into a launch video script, shot list, and caption text.

components.name: Higgsfield Orchestration Service
components.responsibility: Builds Higgsfield API/MCP requests from script+assets, estimates credit cost pre-render, submits render jobs, handles callbacks/polling, retrieves 16:9 and 9:16 outputs.

components.name: Asset Storage (Supabase Storage)
components.responsibility: Stores uploaded screenshots, screen recordings, logos, and final rendered video files/thumbnails.

components.name: Database (Supabase Postgres)
components.responsibility: Persists users, projects, context data, scripts, render jobs, assets, and billing/subscription state.

components.name: Billing Service (Stripe)
components.responsibility: Manages flat-fee subscription plans, payment status, and gates render job creation based on active subscription.

components.name: Auth Service (Supabase Auth)
components.responsibility: Email/password + OAuth login, session management, row-level security policy enforcement.

components.name: Job Worker / Queue
components.responsibility: Background processing for long-running render submission, status polling, caption burning, and multi-format export assembly triggered post-render.

techStack.llm: OpenAI API (or equivalent LLM provider) for context extraction summarization, script/shot-list generation, and publishing-kit copy generation.
techStack.auth: Supabase Auth (email/password + optional GitHub OAuth for future repo-connect), JWT-based session, RLS enforced at the DB layer.
techStack.infra: Vercel for hosting/CI-CD of the Next.js app; Supabase Storage for asset/video file storage; Stripe for subscription billing; Higgsfield API/MCP as the core video-generation provider; Inngest or Trigger.dev for durable background job orchestration and webhook handling.
techStack.backend: Next.js Route Handlers (Node runtime) for API endpoints; background job worker implemented via a queue (Supabase Edge Functions or a lightweight worker service e.g. Inngest/Trigger.dev) for long-running Higgsfield render polling and post-processing.
techStack.database: Supabase Postgres with Row Level Security policies scoping all tables to the authenticated user_id (via project ownership).
techStack.devtools: TypeScript, ESLint/Prettier, Supabase CLI for local dev/migrations, GitHub Actions for CI (lint/build/test), Vercel preview deployments for PR review.
techStack.frontend: Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS, deployed as a single full-stack app; guided multi-step wizard UI with client-side upload progress and job-status polling via SWR/React Query.

tasks.title: Set up Supabase project and schema
tasks.description: Provision Supabase project, run schemaSql migrations for users, subscriptions, projects, project_context, assets, scripts, render_jobs, and publishing_kits, and configure Row Level Security policies scoping all rows to the owning user via project relationships.

tasks.title: Implement auth and subscription gating
tasks.description: Wire up Supabase Auth (email/password) in Next.js, create protected route middleware, integrate Stripe Checkout/webhooks for flat-fee subscription creation, and enforce active-subscription checks before allowing render job creation.

tasks.title: Deploy pipeline setup
tasks.description: Connect repo to Vercel for automatic preview/production deployments, configure environment variables (Supabase keys, Stripe keys, Higgsfield API keys, LLM API keys), and set up GitHub Actions for lint/build checks on PRs.

tasks.title: Build guided intake wizard and asset upload flow
tasks.description: Create the multi-step form (product description, tone, platform, screenshots/screen-recordings/logo upload to Supabase Storage) that creates a Project, ProjectContext, and Asset records.

tasks.title: Build script/shot-list generation and review UI
tasks.description: Implement the LLM-backed endpoint that consumes ProjectContext to generate a Script (script_text, shot_list, captions), plus a review/edit UI where the founder approves or edits before render submission.

tasks.title: Build Higgsfield orchestration and cost-approval flow
tasks.description: Implement the service that builds a Higgsfield render request from the approved Script and Assets, computes estimated_credit_cost for user approval, submits the job, and creates a RenderJob record in pending_approval/queued state.

tasks.title: Build background worker for job polling and multi-format export
tasks.description: Implement a durable background job (Inngest/Trigger.dev or Supabase Edge Function cron) that polls/receives Higgsfield webhooks, updates RenderJob status, fetches 16:9 and 9:16 outputs plus burned-in captions, generates a thumbnail, stores results as Assets, and creates the PublishingKit.

tasks.title: Build job status dashboard and final video delivery UI
tasks.description: Create the project dashboard showing RenderJob status in real time, and once completed, display/download both video formats along with the generated PublishingKit (title, description, hashtags, thumbnail).

openQuestions: What markup on Higgsfield API/credit costs is needed to sustain a $69/mo flat fee without eroding margin, and how should estimated_credit_cost be computed per job type?
Should GitHub repo OAuth be required at signup, or is screenshot-only ingestion sufficient for the 72-hour MVP, and does this change the ProjectContext schema now vs. later?

What minimum codebase signal (README, package.json, live URL) reliably produces accurate narrative extraction within the build window, and should this be validated with a fallback to manual-only input?

Do we proxy/store rendered videos ourselves in Supabase Storage or serve directly from Higgsfield's storage/CDN for v1, and what are the implications for asset retention, egress cost, and long-term URL stability?
How do we handle Higgsfield job failures/retries without double-charging credits, and what user-facing retry/refund policy should the render_jobs.status flow support?

What is the polling vs. webhook strategy for Higgsfield job status, and does the chosen background job framework (Inngest/Trigger.dev/Edge Functions) reliably support the expected render durations (minutes to tens of minutes)?
engineering.schemaSqlExcerpt:
CREATE TABLE projects (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  platform text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'product_hunt',
  tone text,
  product_description text
);

CREATE TABLE project_context (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  readme_text text,
  repo_url text,
  extracted_features jsonb DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb
);
